model.name: Party Role
model.purpose: Represent an actor's functional role as a time-bounded assignment scoped to an object, activity, organisation, resource or process, without encoding the actor's identity, the scoped thing, or the permissions that may be derived from the role.
model.scope_statement: Party Role is a format-neutral mixin for a role assignment: a player (party, agent, device or unnamed occupancy) holds a typed function relative to a scope (object, activity, organisation, resource or process) for a validity interval. The mixin covers identity of the assignment, role classification, player and scope binding, occupancy rules, lifecycle, delegation and on-behalf-of, derived authority, eligibility constraints, evidence, access and alignment to external role codes. It does not own party master data, activity definitions, permission catalogues, credentials, places, or act-performance (participation) events; those remain sibling models. Standing organisational assignments (FHIR PractitionerRole), activity-qualified associations (W3C PROV Association/hadRole), trade-party role codes (UN/CEFACT), payment PartyRole (ISO 20022) and metadata CI_Responsibility (ISO 19115-1) are treated as alignments, not as this model's native storage.
in_scope: Identity of a role-assignment instance, distinct from the player's party identifier and from any date used as a surrogate key.
Functional role type or code, including code-system, version, label, hierarchy and mapping to external vocabularies.
Binding of a player (person, organisation, software agent, device, group, or vacant/unnamed occupancy) to the assignment.
Scope of the role: object, activity, process, organisation, resource, account, payment, dataset or other host entity.
Scoping or authorising entity that defines, employs or certifies the role (HL7 scoper; FHIR organization).
Validity interval, active flag and assignment lifecycle (pending, active, suspended, interim, expired, revoked, historical).
Delegation, agency and on-behalf-of, including ultimate versus immediate parties in a chain.
Occupancy cardinality, exclusive versus shared holding, locum/interim substitution and succession/handover.
Spatial, jurisdictional or service extent of the role, and role-local contact or service context.
Eligibility or licence constraints that condition occupancy, without storing the credential itself.
Evidence, provenance, quality, access, retention and interoperability of role-assignment records.
out_of_scope: Party, person, organisation, legal-entity or agent master identity and demographics.
Activity, process, workflow or event definitions and their execution traces except as scope or participation references.
Permission, privilege, entitlement, access-control policy and RBAC/ABAC decision objects.
Employment contracts, compensation and human-resources legal instruments (HL7 Employee versus AssignedEntity distinction).
Personal, kinship or purely relational links that are not a functional role scoped to an object or activity.
Qualification, licence, training or credential records themselves.
Location or place as a first-class geospatial entity.
Participation or performance of an act (who actually did what in a specific event), except as a linked sibling.
PROV Role applied to non-actor entities (for example a utensil used as a mixing implement).
HL7 RoleClass partitive, ontological and passive-material roles (ingredient, instance-of-kind, owned material).
Ownership as a property right, citizenship, or other civil status except as optional aligned role codes.

boundary_notes.distinction: The player is referenced, not duplicated. HL7 RoleClass treats Role as an association between a playing entity and a scoping entity; FHIR PractitionerRole.practitioner is optional so a role post can exist without a named person. Schema.org Role similarly qualifies a relationship rather than identifying the person.

HL7 RIM and FHIR Provenance separate standing role (competence or assignment) from participation type (how the agent took part in a specific activity). This mixin is the former. ISO 20022 PartyRole on a Payment is closer to participation-in-transaction and is an alignment, not a licence to merge the two concepts.

FHIR Provenance.agent.type is functional participation; Provenance.agent.role is a security-role example binding. Occupying a Party Role does not by itself grant permissions. Authorisation objects belong to a sibling access-control model.

HL7 RoleClass EMP identifies the work-for-compensation relationship; ASSIGNED is the functional role on behalf of an organisation. A party may be employed without holding a given functional role, and a locum may occupy a functional role without being the employer's EMP record.

FHIR states that Practitioner qualifications do not imply a Role. HL7 QUAL is recognition of training or characteristics that would make an entity an appropriate performer; occupancy of this mixin may require such eligibility but must not store the credential.

prov:Role is the function of an entity or agent with respect to an activity in usage, generation, association, start or end. This mixin specialises the actor/agent case and the standing organisational assignment case; it does not model PROV Role on non-agent entities, nor does it replace prov:Association or prov:Plan.

CI_Responsibility is information about the party and their role relative to a metadata resource, with a mandatory CI_RoleCode and optional spatial/temporal extent. It is an alignment for resource-scoped responsible-party roles, not a party master or a permission.

UN/CEFACT partyRoleCode includes codes such as family member, mother and father, and HL7 RoleClass PRS is a personal relationship. Those belong to a relationship sibling unless they are being used as a functional role on a scoped business object (for example next-of-kin contact on a patient record).

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Defines prov:Role as the function of an entity or agent with respect to an activity; prov:Association as assignment of responsibility with optional hadRole, hadPlan and actedOnBehalfOf; and Agent subclasses Person, Organization and SoftwareAgent.

sources.title: FHIR Resource PractitionerRole
sources.relevance: Normative pattern for a standing actor-role assignment: identifiers, active flag, authorised period, practitioner, organisation, role codes, specialty, locations, healthcare services, and explicit boundaries with qualifications and CareTeam.

sources.title: schema.org Role
sources.relevance: Defines Role as an intermediate qualifier on a relationship, with startDate, endDate, roleName and subtypes OrganizationRole and PerformanceRole; demonstrates time-bounded occupancy without conflating player identity.

sources.title: unece:PartyRoleCodeList
sources.organization: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UN/CEFACT)
sources.relevance: Authoritative multi-industry party-role code list (buyer, consignee, carrier, authorised official, temporary employee, agent/representative direct and indirect, and hundreds of trade, transport, energy and healthcare functions).

sources.title: HL7 CodeSystem RoleClass
sources.relevance: Defines Role as association between playing entity and scoping entity; distinguishes AssignedEntity from Employee, Agent/on-behalf-of, signing authority, licensed entity, qualified entity, vacant-capable assigned posts, and excludes partitive/ontological/passive material roles from this mixin.

sources.title: ISO20022 types — Role and PartyRole component restructure
sources.relevance: Describes the ISO 20022 Role component as the association of a Party with another component plus business intention, and the repeating PartyRole element (DebtorRole, CreditorRole, UltimateDebtorRole, AccountOwnerRole and related extensions). Not a substitute for the ISO 20022 Registration Authority dictionary.

sources.title: class CI_Responsibility (ISO 19115-1 metadata)
sources.organization: Intergovernmental Committee on Surveying and Mapping (ICSM), documenting ISO 19115-1
sources.version_or_date: ISO 19115-1:2014 with 2018 amendment as documented by ICSM MDWG
sources.relevance: ISO 19115-1 CI_Responsibility binds party, mandatory CI_RoleCode (function performed by the responsible party) and optional spatial or temporal extent of the role; 2014-to-2018 change replaced CI_ResponsibleParty to allow more flexible party/role associations.

sources.title: unece:partyRoleCode
sources.organization: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UN/CEFACT)
sources.relevance: Defines partyRoleCode as a code specifying the role of a trade party or transport person, ranging over PartyRoleCodeList and domain-typed to TradeParty and TransportPerson.

sources.title: FHIR Resource Provenance
sources.relevance: Maps W3C PROV into FHIR: agent who/onBehalfOf, occurred versus recorded time, participation type versus security role, and constraints that who and onBehalfOf cannot be the same. Distinguishes activity-scoped participation from standing PractitionerRole.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a Party Role assignment is identified and how its functional type is classified independently of storage format.
bundles.rationale: Every interoperable role assignment needs a stable identity distinct from the player and from calendar dates, plus a typed function drawn from a governed code system. W3C, HL7, UN/CEFACT and Schema.org all identify the function separately from the actor.

layers.name: Assignment identity
layers.description: Identifiers and disambiguation for the role-assignment instance rather than for the player or the scope.

findings.name: Role-assignment identifier
findings.description: A Party Role record is an identifiable assignment. FHIR PractitionerRole.identifier holds business identifiers specific to a role/location. Schema.org Role may carry identifier. HL7 Role.id is used for policy-holder and similar role instances. A date is never an identifier.

questions.text: What authoritative master-system identifier uniquely identifies this role assignment?
What governed global IRI or UUID/ULID identifies this assignment when no master-system identifier exists?
How is this assignment identifier kept distinct from the player's party identifier and from any validity date?
Which alternate identifiers (national provider-role numbers, registry keys, sameAs IRIs) alias this assignment?

data_elements.name: Assignment identifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the role-assignment instance in the master system of record.

data_elements.name: Assignment IRI
data_elements.description: Governed IRI for the assignment when published on the web or in a linked-data Dimension.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Fallback unique identifier assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or IRI exists.

data_elements.name: Alternate identifier
data_elements.description: Additional business identifiers for the same assignment, each with scheme and status.

artifacts.name: Role assignment identity record
artifacts.description: Canonical identity payload for one assignment, including master id, IRI, Dimension UUID and aliases.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Prefer master-system identifier; else governed IRI; else Dimension UUID/ULID. Never use a date as identity.

findings.name: Identity priority and collision
findings.description: When two records describe the same occupancy, identity priority and HL7 SAME/SUBY-style subsumption must be explicit. FHIR allows multiple PractitionerRole instances when telecom or availability differ. Collision is not solved by overwriting player identity.

questions.text: When two assignment records appear to describe the same player-scope-type occupancy, which identifier is canonical?
Must differing locations, contacts or services force split assignment records rather than a merged identity?
May the same player hold multiple concurrent assignment identifiers for different scopes or role types?

data_elements.name: Canonical record flag
data_elements.description: Whether this assignment record is the prevailing record among duplicates.

data_elements.name: Subsumed assignment reference
data_elements.description: Assignments subsumed into this canonical record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Collision metadata is inline reference data on the assignment record; no separate artefact type is required beyond the identity record.

layers.name: Role typing
layers.description: Classification of the function played, including code systems, labels and excluded RoleClass branches.

findings.name: Functional role code
findings.description: The typed function of the assignment. FHIR PractitionerRole.code binds an example Practitioner Role value set; UN/CEFACT partyRoleCode ranges over PartyRoleCodeList; ISO 19115-1 requires CI_RoleCode; Schema.org uses roleName as text or URL; PROV leaves Role extension to applications.

questions.text: What role code, code system, version and display name classify this assignment's function?
Which organisation maintains the code list and is the code required, preferred or example-bound in this Dimension?
Are multiple role codes allowed on one assignment, and if so what is the primary code?
How is a locally defined or unlisted function represented without claiming false conformance to an external list?

data_elements.name: Role code
data_elements.description: Coded function of the player relative to the scope.

data_elements.name: Role code system
data_elements.description: URI or identifier of the classification scheme (UN/CEFACT PartyRoleCodeList, CI_RoleCode, FHIR value set, local).

data_elements.name: Role display name
data_elements.description: Human-readable name of the function, corresponding to Schema.org roleName when no code is used.

data_elements.name: Primary code flag
data_elements.description: Whether this code is the primary function when several codes are recorded.

artifacts.name: Adopted role code list snapshot
artifacts.description: Versioned snapshot of the Dimension's allowed role codes and their external mappings.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by code-system URI plus published version or snapshot timestamp, not by a calendar date alone.

findings.name: Role-class kind and exclusions
findings.description: HL7 RoleClass partitions roles into ontological, partitive and associative (mutual/formal versus passive). This mixin is limited to associative actor functions (especially AssignedEntity, Agent, licensed/qualified as constraints). Ingredient, instance-of-kind and owned-material roles are out of scope.

questions.text: Which RoleClass kind (assigned, agent, licensed, other associative) does this assignment instantiate?
Has this record been rejected because it is partitive, ontological or a passive material role?
Is this assignment a functional AssignedEntity role, an EMP employment relationship, or both as separate records?

data_elements.name: Role class kind
data_elements.description: High-level kind of the assignment within the associative actor subset.

data_elements.name: HL7 RoleClass code
data_elements.description: Optional alignment code such as ASSIGNED, AGNT, SGNOFF, LIC, QUAL, EMP.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Kind and exclusion flags are classifiers on the assignment; they are not independent artefacts.

findings.name: Named position and performance label
findings.description: Schema.org distinguishes roleName from the superseded namedPosition and adds PerformanceRole.characterName. A display position (quarterback, inker, attending surgeon) may be more specific than the coded function and must not be treated as an identifier.

questions.text: What named position or performance label further qualifies the coded role?
In which language and script is the role label published, and is there an official translation?
If the label conflicts with the coded function, which value is authoritative for operations?

data_elements.name: Named position
data_elements.description: Free-text or URL position name qualifying the coded role.

data_elements.name: Performance or character label
data_elements.description: Optional label for a performance-scoped role (for example a character name).

findings.inline_only_rationale: Labels are inline text on the assignment; coded functions remain in the adopted code-list artefact.

bundles.name: Player, scope and occupancy
bundles.description: Who plays the role, what object or activity it is scoped to, and whether occupancy is vacant, exclusive or shared.
bundles.rationale: HL7 Role is player plus scoper; FHIR PractitionerRole binds practitioner, organisation, location and service; ISO 19115-1 binds party plus role plus optional extent; ISO 20022 binds Party to a business component via Role. Occupancy rules, including unnamed posts, are first-class.

layers.name: Player binding
layers.description: The actor who occupies, or the explicit vacancy of, the role assignment.

findings.name: Player party binding
findings.description: The player is a reference to a party, person, organisation, software agent, device, group or care-team. PROV Agent may be Person, Organization or SoftwareAgent. FHIR Provenance.agent.who may be Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, CareTeam, Patient, Device or RelatedPerson. This mixin stores the reference, not the party master.

questions.text: Which party, agent, device or group is the player of this assignment?
Is the player a person, organisation, software agent, device, group, care-team or other agent class?
Is the player reference resolvable in the adopting Dimension, or only an unambiguous external identifier?

data_elements.name: Player reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the occupying party or agent.

data_elements.name: Player kind
data_elements.description: Class of the player (person, organisation, software-agent, device, group, care-team, other).

data_elements.name: Unresolved player identifier
data_elements.description: Unambiguous identifier when the player is not a resolvable local party.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Player is a reference to a sibling Party/Agent record or an external identifier; no extra artefact is required.

findings.name: Vacant, unnamed and non-person players
findings.description: FHIR explicitly allows PractitionerRole with an empty Practitioner for an un-named surgeon at a named organisation. PROV and FHIR Provenance allow device and software agents. Vacancy is a first-class occupancy state, not a missing identity. Collective players (group, care-team) are allowed when the Dimension treats the group as the actor.

questions.text: Is this assignment vacant or unnamed, and is vacancy permitted for this role type and scope?
If the player is a device or software agent, what identifies it and under whose organisational scope does it act?
Is the player a group or care-team rather than an individual, and how is individual contribution recorded if needed?
Has a non-actor UN/CEFACT code such as animal-being-investigated been offered, and should it be rejected as out of scope?

data_elements.name: Vacant occupancy flag
data_elements.description: True when the assignment exists without a named player.

data_elements.name: Unnamed player allowed
data_elements.description: Policy flag copied onto the instance indicating unnamed occupancy is valid for this post.

data_elements.name: Collective player reference
data_elements.description: Group or care-team occupying the role when the actor is not an individual.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Vacancy and player-kind flags are inline state of the assignment.

layers.name: Scope binding
layers.description: The object, activity, organisation or resource that the role is scoped to, plus optional spatial or service extent.

findings.name: Scoped object or activity
findings.description: A Party Role is meaningless without a scope. PROV hadRole is always in the context of an activity (association, usage, generation, start, end). ISO 20022 Role associates a Party with another business component (Payment, Account, Obligation). FHIR PractitionerRole is scoped by organisation and optionally location and HealthcareService. ISO 19115-1 CI_Responsibility is scoped by the metadata resource or process step.

questions.text: What object, activity, process, resource, account or other host is this role scoped to?
Is the scope an activity, a standing organisation, a resource/dataset, a financial component, or another host kind?
If no scope is recorded, is the assignment invalid or is a default Dimension-wide scope authorised?

data_elements.name: Scope reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the object, activity, organisation, resource or component that the role is about.

data_elements.name: Scope kind
data_elements.description: Kind of scoped host (activity, organisation, resource, account, payment, process-step, other).

findings.inline_only_rationale: Scope is a reference to a sibling entity or activity; the mixin does not store the host.

findings.name: Scoping entity and organisation
findings.description: HL7 Role.scoper is the entity that defines or authorises the role (employer, licence issuer, represented party). FHIR organization is where the roles are available and need not be the direct employer. PROV actedOnBehalfOf links an agent to a represented agent. These are distinct from the scoped object when the object is an activity or dataset.

questions.text: Which entity scopes, employs, licences or is represented by this role?
Is the scoping organisation different from the player's employer, and is that expected?
Does this role exist on the player's own authority with no scoper, as HL7 allows for clinical research sponsor?

data_elements.name: Scoper reference
data_elements.description: Organisation or party that scopes or authorises the role.

data_elements.name: Self-scoped flag
data_elements.description: True when the player undertakes the role on its own authority.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Scoper is a party reference; inline on the assignment.

findings.name: Spatial and service extent
findings.description: ISO 19115-1 added CI_Responsibility.extent so a role may have spatial or temporal extent. FHIR PractitionerRole.location and healthcareService constrain where and for which services the role applies. This mixin references place and service siblings rather than embedding geometries.

questions.text: At which locations or spatial extents may this role be exercised?
Which services, specialties or functions are in scope for this assignment?
Which legal or administrative jurisdiction bounds the role, analogous to HL7 territory-of-authority?

data_elements.name: Location reference
data_elements.description: Places at which the role may be performed.

data_elements.name: Geographic extent
data_elements.description: Optional spatial extent of the role as defined by a sibling extent model.

data_elements.name: Specialty or service
data_elements.description: Service or specialty codes that further restrict the assignment.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction code
data_elements.description: Legal or administrative jurisdiction of the role.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Extent and location are references or inline codes; geometries live in a sibling location/extent model.

layers.name: Occupancy rules
layers.description: How many players may occupy a post, whether codes may repeat, and role-local contact context.

findings.name: Cardinality, exclusivity and sharing
findings.description: Standards conflict on occupancy. Some ISO 19115 profiles require a single CI_RoleCode per CI_Responsibility. FHIR allows 0..* role codes on one PractitionerRole and multiple PractitionerRole instances. Schema.org Role qualifies one relationship instance. Job-share, exclusive posts and many-codes-one-assignment must be explicit Dimension policy.

questions.text: Is occupancy of this post exclusive, shared, or limited to a maximum number of concurrent players?
Does this Dimension require exactly one role code per assignment record, contrary to FHIR 0..* codes?
May the same player hold two assignments of the same role type on the same scope at the same time?

data_elements.name: Exclusivity
data_elements.description: Occupancy rule: exclusive, shared, or bounded.

data_elements.name: Maximum concurrent players
data_elements.description: Upper bound on simultaneous occupants when the post is shared.

data_elements.name: Single code required
data_elements.description: Whether the Dimension forbids multiple role codes on one assignment.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Occupancy constraints are policy values on the assignment or its role-type template.

findings.name: Role-local contact and service context
findings.description: FHIR records telecom, availability and endpoints on PractitionerRole because they belong to the post, not the person. ISO 19115-1 CI_Party carries contactInfo for the responsible party in that role. Role-local channels must not overwrite party-master contacts.

questions.text: What contact channels, endpoints or availability windows belong to this assignment rather than to the player master?
When role-local contact differs from party-master contact, which must operational systems use?
Does a change of telecom or availability require a new assignment record, as FHIR recommends when details are not uniform?

data_elements.name: Role-local contact
data_elements.description: Contact points that apply while occupying this role.

data_elements.name: Role endpoint
data_elements.description: Electronic service endpoint associated with the assignment.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role-local contacts are inline structured values or references to a contact sibling; they are not independent artefacts unless issued as a public directory extract.

bundles.name: Lifecycle and time
bundles.description: Validity intervals, event versus observation time, assignment states, succession and historical occupancy.
bundles.rationale: Schema.org Role and FHIR PractitionerRole are explicitly time-bounded. FHIR Provenance and W3C PROV separate when an activity occurred from when it was recorded. Rare cases include interim/locum, suspended, revoked and post-end historical occupancy.

layers.name: Temporal bounds
layers.description: Start, end and the distinction between effective time and record time.

findings.name: Validity period
findings.description: FHIR PractitionerRole.period is the interval during which the person is authorised to act in the role for the organisation. Schema.org Role uses startDate and endDate. Open-ended assignments omit end. All timestamps in this mixin use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

questions.text: When did this assignment become effective, with seconds and explicit timezone?
When does or did authorisation end, or is the assignment open-ended?
Do planned start/end differ from actual start/end, and which pair governs operations?

data_elements.name: Valid from
data_elements.description: Effective start of the assignment as RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Valid to
data_elements.description: Effective end of the assignment as RFC 3339 date-time; absent if open-ended.

data_elements.name: Open-ended flag
data_elements.description: True when no end is authorised.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Period values are inline timestamps on the assignment.

findings.name: Event time versus observation time
findings.description: FHIR Provenance.occurred is when the activity happened; Provenance.recorded is when it was recorded. W3C PROV similarly distinguishes activity start/end from later attribution. Role assignment, suspension, handover and revocation each have an event time and a possibly later ingestion/observation time.

questions.text: When did the lifecycle event (assign, suspend, revoke, handover) actually occur?
When was that event observed or ingested into this Dimension?
If event time is after recorded time or lacks an offset, how is the record invalidated or corrected?

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: Instant the lifecycle event occurred, RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Recorded time
data_elements.description: Instant the event was recorded or ingested, RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Event kind
data_elements.description: Kind of lifecycle event (assign, activate, suspend, resume, revoke, expire, handover, correct).

artifacts.name: Role lifecycle event record
artifacts.description: Serial event that changes assignment state, carrying event time, recorded time, actor and reason.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Event identifier from the originating workflow system if present; otherwise Dimension ULID. Event time is not the identifier.

layers.name: Assignment states
layers.description: Active, pending, suspended, interim, expired, revoked and historical occupancy, including succession.

findings.name: Assignment status lifecycle
findings.description: FHIR PractitionerRole.active marks whether the record is in active use, including marking practitioners not currently employed. Additional states needed in the wide union include pending credential, suspended, revoked, expired, and interim. Status is not implied by dates alone.

questions.text: What is the current status of this assignment (pending, active, suspended, expired, revoked, historical)?
If active is false while the period still contains now, which field governs operational authorisation?
Which status transitions are legal, and which require a recorded lifecycle event and authorising agent?

data_elements.name: Assignment status
data_elements.description: Lifecycle status of the assignment.

data_elements.name: Active flag
data_elements.description: Whether the assignment record is in active use.

data_elements.name: Status reason
data_elements.description: Coded or textual reason for the current status.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status is inline on the assignment; transitions are recorded as lifecycle-event artefacts.

findings.name: Succession, interim and locum
findings.description: UN/CEFACT includes temporary employee. FHIR period supports locum windows. Wide-union operating practice needs predecessor/successor links, acting-up flags and handover events so a post is never silently double-filled or left without a responsible occupant. Primary support for a universal handover object is limited; treat detailed handover workflow as a Dimension process on top of this mixin.

questions.text: Which assignment does this one succeed, and was there a handover overlap or a gap?
Is this occupant interim, acting, or a locum, and does the incumbent assignment remain active?
When was responsibility handed over, by whom, and what residual duties remain with the predecessor?

data_elements.name: Occupancy mode
data_elements.description: substantive, interim, acting, locum, job-share or other mode.

data_elements.name: Predecessor assignment
data_elements.description: Assignment this record succeeds.

data_elements.name: Incumbent assignment
data_elements.description: Standing assignment remaining in force during locum or acting occupancy.

artifacts.name: Role handover record
artifacts.description: Optional process artefact documenting transfer of a post between assignments. Primary standards specify period and status more strongly than a universal handover document; Dimensions should treat this as a local process artefact.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Workflow-system identifier if present; otherwise Dimension ULID.

findings.name: Historical occupancy after end
findings.description: Ended assignments remain queryable for audit, provenance and ISO 19115 responsible-party history. Revocation is not physical deletion. Posthumous or post-dissolution occupancy may remain historically true (author, originator) while active is false.

questions.text: Must ended assignments remain visible for a given as-of time, and to which access roles?
Was the assignment revoked for cause, expired by period, or superseded by succession?
Does this historical role remain citable (author, originator, rights holder) after the player can no longer act?

data_elements.name: End kind
data_elements.description: expired, revoked, superseded, vacated or other.

data_elements.name: Historically visible
data_elements.description: Whether the ended assignment remains in as-of queries.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Historical flags are inline; retention schedules are Dimension policy rather than a separate artefact type.

bundles.name: Authority, delegation and constraints
bundles.description: On-behalf-of chains, signing and commissioning authority, eligibility versus occupancy, conflicts, and the boundary with permissions.
bundles.rationale: PROV actedOnBehalfOf, FHIR Provenance.onBehalfOf, HL7 AGNT/SGNOFF/COMPAR/LIC/QUAL, ISO 20022 ultimate parties and UN/CEFACT direct versus indirect representation all show that function, agency and permission are separable.

layers.name: Agency and delegation
layers.description: Who the player represents and how ultimate versus immediate parties are distinguished.

findings.name: On-behalf-of and ultimate party
findings.description: PROV actedOnBehalfOf and qualified Delegation record that an agent acted for another. FHIR Provenance.agent.onBehalfOf is the delegating agent and must not equal who. ISO 20022 distinguishes Debtor/Creditor from UltimateDebtor/UltimateCreditor for payments on behalf of another. UN/CEFACT distinguishes direct and indirect representation. Chains must be explicit.

questions.text: On whose behalf is this player occupying the role, and is that party different from the player?
Who is the ultimate party versus the immediate party in this agency chain?
Is representation direct or indirect, as in UN/CEFACT DEN/DEO, and what instrument authorises it?
What plan, mandate or power-of-attorney, if any, did the agent follow (PROV hadPlan)?

data_elements.name: On-behalf-of reference
data_elements.description: Party or agent that delegated authority to the player.

data_elements.name: Ultimate party reference
data_elements.description: Ultimate originator or beneficiary when different from the immediate player.

data_elements.name: Representation mode
data_elements.description: direct, indirect, or unspecified representation.

data_elements.name: Plan or mandate reference
data_elements.description: Plan, mandate or instrument the agent intended to follow.

artifacts.name: Delegation or representation instrument
artifacts.description: Power of attorney, mandate, agency agreement or PROV Plan that authorises on-behalf-of occupancy.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Instrument identifier from the issuing authority if present; otherwise hash-backed Dimension identifier.

findings.name: Signing and commissioning authority
findings.description: HL7 SGNOFF is the officer or signature authority for a scoping entity. COMPAR is a commissioning party authorised to issue permissions or credentials. These are actor roles with extra authority semantics, not the permission objects themselves. FHIR Provenance uses legal authenticator as a participation type on an activity.

questions.text: May this assignment legally sign or authenticate acts for the scoper, and for which act classes?
May this assignment issue credentials, privileges or further role assignments?
What value, jurisdiction or subject-matter limits bind the signing or commissioning authority?

data_elements.name: Signing authority flag
data_elements.description: Whether the assignment includes signature or authentication authority.

data_elements.name: Commissioning authority flag
data_elements.description: Whether the assignment may instantiate permissions, credentials or further roles.

data_elements.name: Authority limit
data_elements.description: Structured limits on signing or commissioning.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Authority flags and limits are inline on the assignment; the actual signed artefacts belong to sibling document or provenance models.

layers.name: Eligibility and conflicts
layers.description: Constraints that condition occupancy without turning the mixin into a credential or permission catalogue.

findings.name: Eligibility versus occupancy
findings.description: FHIR: qualifications do not imply a Role. HL7 QUAL is recognition that would make an entity an appropriate performer; LIC is scoper-certified authorisation to perform activities under a jurisdiction. Occupancy may require referenced credentials to be valid at event time, but this mixin stores references and expiry checks, not the credential body.

questions.text: Which credentials, licences or qualifications must be valid for this occupancy, and who is the issuing scoper?
If a required credential expires while the assignment period is still open, does occupancy auto-suspend?
Is the player eligible but not occupying, and should eligibility be recorded only on the credential sibling?

data_elements.name: Required credential reference
data_elements.description: Credential or licence that must be valid during occupancy.

data_elements.name: Auto-suspend on credential expiry
data_elements.description: Whether occupancy suspends when a required credential expires.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Eligibility is a set of references to a credential sibling plus inline policy flags.

findings.name: Incompatible and conflict roles
findings.description: A player may hold many concurrent roles. Some pairs are incompatible (for example ISO 20022 who versus onBehalfOf identity; auditor versus auditee; FHIR who must not equal onBehalfOf). A universal conflict catalogue was not found in the primary sources; Dimensions must declare local incompatibilities rather than claim a global matrix.

questions.text: Which other assignments of this player are declared incompatible with this occupancy?
Does this assignment violate the who-not-equal-onBehalfOf rule or a local anti-self-dealing rule?
Is a documented exception (Chinese wall, recusal, time-box) in force for an otherwise forbidden pair?

data_elements.name: Incompatibility code
data_elements.description: Local code naming a forbidden role pair or self-dealing pattern.

data_elements.name: Conflict exception reference
data_elements.description: Authorised exception that permits an otherwise incompatible occupancy.

artifacts.name: Role-conflict exception record
artifacts.description: Documented recusal, Chinese-wall or time-boxed exception to an incompatibility rule.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision identifier from the authorising body; else Dimension ULID.

findings.name: Permission boundary
findings.description: Occupying a Party Role does not mint permissions. FHIR Provenance.agent.role is a security-role example, distinct from agent.type (functional participation) and from PractitionerRole. Any authorisation implied by a post must be realised in a sibling access-control model, with an optional traceability link.

questions.text: Which permission or policy objects, if any, are derived from this assignment in the access-control sibling?
Does this Dimension forbid treating role occupancy as an implicit access grant?
What purpose-of-use or authorisation context, if any, accompanies this assignment when it is used in an activity?

data_elements.name: Derived permission reference
data_elements.description: Optional link to permissions realised from this assignment.

data_elements.name: Implicit grant forbidden
data_elements.description: Policy flag that occupancy does not itself grant access.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The permission boundary is a policy flag plus optional references; permission objects are out of scope.

bundles.name: Evidence, access and interoperability
bundles.description: Provenance of the assignment, quality, access and retention of role records, and mappings to external standards including known conflicts.
bundles.rationale: Role assignments are themselves records with provenance (W3C PROV, FHIR Provenance). They may contain individual-category data (FHIR PractitionerRole security category Individual). External code systems do not agree, so alignments must record conflicts rather than claim conformance.

layers.name: Provenance and quality
layers.description: Who asserted the assignment, on what evidence, and with what verification.

findings.name: Assignment provenance and instruments
findings.description: Creating or changing a Party Role is an activity with agents. FHIR Provenance.target can point at a PractitionerRole. Instruments include appointment letters, board minutes, contracts and mandates. W3C PROV allows attribution, association and delegation on that activity.

questions.text: Who asserted or authorised this assignment, and on whose behalf?
What instrument or source record evidences the assignment?
Is there a provenance-of-provenance bundle for this assignment, and what is its identifier?

data_elements.name: Asserting agent
data_elements.description: Agent who created or authorised the assignment record.

data_elements.name: Instrument reference
data_elements.description: Evidence instrument for the assignment.

data_elements.name: Provenance record reference
data_elements.description: Link to a PROV or FHIR Provenance record about this assignment.

artifacts.name: Appointment or assignment instrument
artifacts.description: Letter, minute, contract clause or registry extract that evidences occupancy.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuing-authority instrument identifier if present; else content digest plus Dimension ULID.

findings.name: Quality and verification
findings.description: ISO 19115-1 roles such as processor, editor and custodian exist because responsible-party claims affect dataset trust. FHIR Provenance is used to assess authenticity and reliability. Role records need verification status, completeness of player/scope/code, and an explicit non-conformance flag when mappings are approximate.

questions.text: Has this assignment been verified, by whom, and at what time?
Which mandatory elements (player or vacancy, scope, role code, period or open-ended flag) are missing?
If the role code is mapped from an external system, what is the mapping confidence and residual mismatch?

data_elements.name: Verification status
data_elements.description: unverified, verified, disputed or withdrawn.

data_elements.name: Mapping confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence that an aligned external code matches this assignment's function.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Quality flags are inline; verification events reuse the lifecycle-event artefact.

layers.name: Access and retention
layers.description: Who may read or change role records, and how long occupancy history is kept.

findings.name: Access, privacy and exceptions
findings.description: FHIR PractitionerRole has security category Individual. Role records can reveal employment, licence and contact data. Default access should be need-to-know by scope, with break-glass and public-directory exceptions (ISO 19115 pointOfContact, publisher).

questions.text: Who may read this assignment at bundle, layer, finding and artefact scope?
Is this assignment published in a public point-of-contact or provider directory exception?
Which player or contact fields must be redacted in secondary use?

data_elements.name: Access classification
data_elements.description: Sensitivity classification of the assignment record.

data_elements.name: Public directory flag
data_elements.description: Whether selected fields are published as a point of contact.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Access flags are inline; access-control decisions remain in the sibling permission model.

findings.name: Retention and deletion
findings.description: Ended assignments are retained for audit and provenance. Legal retention (clinical, financial, public records) is jurisdictional. Deletion of an active occupancy should be refused in favour of revocation. Right-to-erasure may require redaction of player fields while preserving that a role post existed.

questions.text: How long must this assignment and its lifecycle events be retained after end or revocation?
Is physical deletion forbidden while revocation or historical retention is required?
If a player requests erasure, which assignment fields may be redacted without destroying the role-post audit trail?

data_elements.name: Retain until
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant after which deletion or anonymisation may be considered.

data_elements.name: Deletion forbidden
data_elements.description: True when physical delete is not permitted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention timestamps and flags are inline Dimension policy on the assignment.

layers.name: External alignment
layers.description: Mappings to PROV, FHIR, UN/CEFACT, ISO 20022 and ISO 19115, plus the participation distinction.

findings.name: External code alignment and conflicts
findings.description: The same English word (owner, agent, processor, author) is not equivalent across CI_RoleCode, UN/CEFACT PartyRoleCodeList, FHIR Practitioner Role, ISO 20022 PartyRole subtypes and prov:Role. Alignments are directional maps with conflict notes. Conformance to any one list is a Dimension claim, not a property of this mixin.

questions.text: Which external codes (UN/CEFACT, CI_RoleCode, FHIR, ISO 20022, PROV) are mapped to this assignment, and in which direction?
What semantic conflicts are known for this mapping (for example owner as property versus owner as account party)?
Does this Dimension claim conformance to a named external role list, and what evidence supports that claim?

data_elements.name: External mapping
data_elements.description: One mapped external code with system, direction and conflict note.

data_elements.name: Conformance target
data_elements.description: Named external list to which a Dimension optionally claims conformance.

artifacts.name: Role concept map
artifacts.description: Versioned map among UN/CEFACT, CI_RoleCode, FHIR, ISO 20022 and local codes, with conflict annotations.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Map identifier plus map version; never a date alone.

findings.name: Participation versus role boundary
findings.description: Standing Party Role occupancy is not a statement that the player performed a particular act. FHIR Provenance.agent.type records how an agent participated in an activity; PractitionerRole records what the practitioner may perform for an organisation over a period. ISO 20022 PartyRole on a Payment is activity-instance scoped and should be linked as participation-like use of this mixin, not stored as a second identity model.

questions.text: Is this record a standing assignment or an activity-instance participation, and which sibling holds the other?
If linked to a participation, what participation type (performer, author, enterer, verifier) applies to the activity?
Does this Dimension forbid merging standing occupancy and act-participation into a single undifferentiated role record?

data_elements.name: Assignment mode
data_elements.description: standing-assignment or activity-instance.

data_elements.name: Participation reference
data_elements.description: Optional link to a participation sibling for a specific activity.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The participation boundary is a mode flag plus a sibling reference.

functions.name: Assign party role
functions.description: Create a new role-assignment instance binding player (or vacancy), scope, role type and validity, with provenance.
preconditions: Scope exists or is an authorised external identifier.
Role code is in the adopted list or explicitly marked local.
Vacancy policy allows unnamed occupancy if player is absent.
No exclusive-occupancy collision exists unless an exception is recorded.
effects: A new assignment record exists in pending or active status.
Event time and recorded time are stored separately.
Optional instrument and asserting agent are linked.

functions.name: Activate or suspend role
functions.description: Change assignment status between pending, active and suspended without ending the period.
preconditions: Assignment exists and is not revoked or deleted.
Authorising agent holds commissioning or registrar authority.
Required credentials are valid if activating.
effects: Operational authorisation follows status, not period alone.

functions.name: Revoke or end role
functions.description: End occupancy by expiry, revocation or vacation while retaining historical visibility according to policy.
outputs: updated assignment with valid_to and end_kind
preconditions: Assignment is pending, active or suspended.
Physical deletion is not requested, or is refused by retention policy.
effects: Status becomes expired, revoked or vacated.
Record remains historically queryable unless a lawful erasure redacts player fields.

functions.name: Handover party role
functions.description: Succeed one assignment with another, optionally as locum/interim with overlap or gap recorded.
preconditions: Exclusivity policy is satisfied by the overlap rule.
Successor player is eligible if credentials are required.
effects: Predecessor may remain incumbent during locum or is ended if substantive succession.

functions.name: Delegate on behalf of
functions.description: Record that the player occupies the role as agent of another party, with optional plan or mandate.
preconditions: on_behalf_of_ref is not the same party as player_ref.
Mandate is valid at event time if required by policy.
effects: Ultimate versus immediate party can be derived when chained.

functions.name: Resolve role at time
functions.description: Query occupants of a scope and role type at an as-of instant, including vacant posts and historical occupancy.
preconditions: Caller is authorised to read at the requested access scope.
as_of_time is RFC 3339 with offset or Z.
effects: No write; returns the as-of occupancy set using period, status and exclusivity rules.

functions.name: Detect role conflict
functions.description: Evaluate incompatible pairs, self-delegation and exclusive-occupancy collisions for a player or post.
preconditions: Incompatibility rules are configured for the Dimension. Absence of a global matrix is expected.
effects: Conflicts are reported; optionally block activate-or-suspend-role.

functions.name: Align external role code
functions.description: Map a local assignment code to or from UN/CEFACT, CI_RoleCode, FHIR, ISO 20022 or PROV without asserting unearned conformance.
preconditions: A versioned concept map exists for the target system.
Local code is not silently rewritten.
effects: Alignment objects are attached; conformance_target remains unset unless evidence is supplied.

composition.purpose: Party Role attaches to a player identity; it does not store demographics. Player may be vacant.
Scope may be an activity; PROV hadRole is activity-contextual. Activity definitions remain a sibling.
Link standing occupancy to who actually performed an act without merging the two concepts.
Scoping or employing organisation that makes the role available or authorises it.
Where the role may be exercised; ISO 19115-1 role extent and FHIR location.
Eligibility constraints on occupancy; credentials are not implied by and not stored as the role.
Optional derivation of authorisation objects; occupancy must not silently grant access.
Align standing or activity-qualified actor roles with prov:Association, prov:hadRole and prov:actedOnBehalfOf.
Align standing healthcare provider-role assignments including period, organisation, location and services.
Align player/scoper semantics and kinds such as ASSIGNED, AGNT, SGNOFF, LIC and QUAL, excluding partitive and ontological branches.
Align trade, transport and multi-industry function codes; reject non-actor codes unless reclassified.
Align repeating PartyRole on payments, accounts and obligations, including ultimate parties; treat as activity-instance-leaning alignment.
Align responsible-party function on datasets and process steps, including role extent.
Align time-bounded relationship qualification, roleName and named position.
Validity and event/recorded timestamps using RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z.
Assignment identity using master-system identifier, then IRI, then Dimension UUID/ULID.

owner_package_requirements: Designate an owner package responsible for Party Role templates, adopted code lists and occupancy policies.
Declare the master identity system for assignments and the IRI namespace if records are published.
Publish vacancy, exclusivity, credential-auto-suspend and implicit-grant-forbidden policies before go-live.
Keep role-type catalogues versioned and separate from party master data.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-owned IRI stem for assignment instances and a separate stem for adopted role-type concepts; do not reuse player IRIs as assignment IRIs. Align, do not copy, UN/CEFACT, CI_RoleCode, FHIR and ISO 20022 URIs.
registry_links: vr.wm-xct-023 Party Role mixin in the Vercy world-model registry
Adopted role code-list registry (UN/CEFACT PartyRoleCodeList and local extensions)
Sibling registries for Party, Activity, Participation, Credential, Location and Permission

canonicalization_rules: Canonical key of a standing assignment is (scope_ref, role_code or primary_role_code, player_ref or vacant token, valid_from if the Dimension splits on period).
Timestamps canonicalise to RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z.
Role codes canonicalise as code-system URI plus code; display names are not identity.
who/player and on_behalf_of cannot canonicalise to the same party.
patch_rules: Patches to player, scope or primary role code on an active assignment require a lifecycle event and may instead create a successor assignment.
Contact and availability patches may require split records when values are not uniform across locations or services.
Status patches cannot silently rewrite valid_from/valid_to.
compatibility_rules: Readers must accept both standing-assignment and activity-instance modes without merging them.
Unknown external mapped codes are retained as alignments, not dropped.
Absence of end date means open-ended, not unknown.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier of the assignment or instrument.
Governed global IRI for the assignment, code list or concept map.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.
A date or validity instant is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event, recorded, valid_from, valid_to and retain_until values SHALL use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; store event time and observation/ingestion time separately.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts (identity records, lifecycle events, handover records, concept-map versions, instruments) use {artefact-kind}-{master-or-ulid}-v{n} without embedding calendar dates as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Instruments and concept maps SHOULD carry a content digest; provenance records SHOULD reference the assignment identifier they describe; redaction for erasure MUST NOT rewrite historical event identifiers.

policies: Occupancy does not imply permission; implicit access grants are forbidden unless a sibling permission object is explicitly derived.
Qualifications and licences do not imply occupancy; occupancy may auto-suspend when a required credential expires if that policy is set.
Physical deletion of role history is refused in favour of revocation plus retention; lawful erasure redacts player fields while preserving that a post existed.
External alignments never constitute a conformance claim without recorded evidence.

read: Authorised callers may resolve assignments by identifier, player, scope, role code and as-of time, including vacant and historical records they are entitled to see.
Public-directory exceptions may expose designated point-of-contact fields only.
create: Registrars or commissioning agents may create assignments when scope, role type and vacancy/exclusivity policies are satisfied.
Create always writes an assign lifecycle event with event time and recorded time.
update: Status, contacts, mappings and delegation fields may be patched under patch_rules.
Changes to player, scope or primary code on an active post SHOULD be modelled as handover or successor create.
delete: Delete is not used for revocation; use revoke-or-end-role.
Physical delete is allowed only after retain_until and only if no legal hold applies, optionally after player-field redaction.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Owns this mixin package, namespace and AGENTS.md bootstrap.
Approves adopted code lists and occupancy policies.

roles.name: Role registrar
responsibilities: Ensures identity priority and vacancy rules are applied.

roles.name: Commissioning authority
responsibilities: Authorises occupancy, signing limits and further role issuance where COMPAR-like authority applies.

roles.name: Alignment steward
responsibilities: Maintains the role concept map and conflict notes.

roles.name: Auditor
responsibilities: Verifies event versus recorded time and retention holds.

roles.name: Player subject
responsibilities: May read their own assignments subject to local law.
May request correction or erasure of player fields without destroying post history.

access.default_rule: Need-to-know by scope and assigning organisation; PractitionerRole-class records default to Individual sensitivity unless a public-directory exception applies.
exceptions: Public point-of-contact or provider-directory publication of named fields.
Break-glass emergency read of active occupancy for a scoped activity, fully audited.
Lawful erasure redaction of player fields while preserving assignment identifiers and lifecycle events.
audit_requirements: All create, status change, handover, delegation and break-glass reads emit a lifecycle or provenance event with event_time, recorded_time and agent.
who/player and on_behalf_of inequality is validated and failures are logged.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md Name, Type and Specification URL to identify this mixin.
Read Storage type URL and Interface URL before any CRUD.
Read Processes URL for assign, handover, revoke and conflict-detection procedures.
Then read adopted role code-list and occupancy policies referenced from the specification.

coverage.claim: This mixin covers the defensible operating surface of an actor role scoped to an object or activity, grounded in W3C PROV-O, HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole and Provenance, HL7 RoleClass, UN/CEFACT partyRoleCode, Schema.org Role and ISO 19115-1 CI_Responsibility, with ISO 20022 PartyRole as a documented secondary alignment. It does not claim a single global role ontology or metaphysical completeness.

checklist.notes: Assignment identifiers distinct from player identifiers; master IRI then Dimension UUID/ULID; dates excluded as identifiers.
pending/active/suspended/expired/revoked/historical plus locum/interim succession; FHIR active and period.
player, scoper, scope, on-behalf-of, predecessor/successor, participation link, credential and permission references.
valid_from/valid_to, open-ended, planned versus actual, event time versus recorded time, RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.
Asserting agent, instruments, PROV/FHIR Provenance links, provenance-of-provenance.
Scoper versus player versus Dimension owner of the record; ISO 19115 owner as a role code is alignment only, not property-right ownership.
Mandatory scope and role code, vacancy policy, who≠onBehalfOf, credential checks, completeness.
Need-to-know default, Individual sensitivity, public-directory and break-glass exceptions, audit.
Revoke-not-delete, retain_until, lawful erasure redaction of player fields, historical visibility.
Concept map to UN/CEFACT, CI_RoleCode, FHIR, ISO 20022 and PROV with explicit conflicts and no unearned conformance.
Vacant/unnamed posts, exclusivity versus sharing, collective and device players.
on-behalf-of, ultimate versus immediate party, direct/indirect representation, hadPlan/mandate.
Functional role codes, RoleClass kind exclusions, named position labels, standing versus activity-instance mode.

known_omissions: EDM Council FIBO PartyInRole / agent-in-role was discovered but the ontology viewer page did not yield a citable class definition in this run; treat FIBO as an ungrounded alignment candidate.
NIST RBAC / INCITS 359 and ABAC (SP 800-162) were not fetched; permission objects remain a sibling and a dedicated RBAC alignment is a gap.
GDPR controller/processor and eIDAS representative powers were not taken from legislative text; legal-capacity roles are a regional gap.
Verifiable Credentials for role occupancy are emerging and lack a primary source in this bundle.
A universal role-conflict matrix does not exist in the cited sources; incompatibilities are Dimension-local.
RACI, Open Contracting party roles and GLEIF relationship records were not grounded.
Robotics-specific operator roles were out of demand (factor_robotics 0.00) and are omitted.
UN/CEFACT list is much larger than the findings enumerate; adopting Dimensions must snapshot the list rather than rely on this mixin to enumerate every code.
conflicts: ISO 19115 profiles that require exactly one CI_RoleCode per CI_Responsibility conflict with FHIR PractitionerRole.code 0..*.
HL7 EMP (employment) versus ASSIGNED (functional role) versus Schema.org OrganizationRole (membership qualifier) are not equivalent.
ISO 20022 PartyRole on a payment instance leans toward participation-in-transaction; FHIR PractitionerRole is a standing assignment; merging them loses meaning.
PROV Role may apply to non-agent entities; this mixin refuses that case.
FHIR Provenance.agent.type (functional participation) versus agent.role (security role example) versus PractitionerRole.code (standing function) are three different classifiers.
English labels such as owner, agent, processor and author are not portable across CI_RoleCode, UN/CEFACT and ISO 20022 without a conflict-annotated map.
IBM documentation of ISO 20022 Role is secondary; it may lag the Registration Authority dictionary.
regional_assumptions: Healthcare licensing and PractitionerRole usage are jurisdiction-specific; FHIR example bindings are not a world code list.
ISO 19115-1 responsible-party practice is described via ICSM (Australia) guidance; other profiles may constrain CI_RoleCode differently.
UN/CEFACT trade roles assume cross-border commercial process semantics that may not fit domestic public-sector posts.
Retention, erasure and public-directory publication depend on local public-records, employment and data-protection law.
Company-officer and signing-authority roles (SGNOFF) vary by corporate law and were not taken from a specific companies statute.
adversarial_checks: A date must never be accepted as assignment identity even if it uniquely locates a posting in a local spreadsheet.
An empty player is valid vacancy, not a data-quality error, when unnamed occupancy is authorised.
Holding EMP or a qualification must not auto-create this mixin occupancy.
A PROV Role on a non-agent entity (the mixing-implement case) must be rejected as out of scope.
Occupancy must not be treated as an access grant without a sibling permission object.
who/player equal to onBehalfOf must fail validation.
Claiming conformance to UN/CEFACT or ISO 19115 solely because a display name matches is forbidden without a versioned map and evidence.
Physical delete of an active assignment must be refused in favour of revoke-or-end-role.
